title: Reaching the Out-of-Pocket Maximum on the Pharmacy Benefit Plan
content:
Once a member's out-of-pocket met reaches the individual out-of-pocket maximum of their Pharmacy Benefit Plan design, or the family reaches the family out-of-pocket maximum under the plan's family accumulation rule, every further covered claim in the same plan year is charged zero member cost share.

## The claim that crosses the maximum

A claim that crosses the maximum is charged only the out-of-pocket remaining, and the out-of-pocket posting equals that remainder. The individual out-of-pocket remaining is the individual maximum less the out-of-pocket met, and never less than zero.

## What is still charged after the maximum

Amounts that never count toward out-of-pocket are still charged after the maximum is reached:

- the brand-generic difference, while the design does not count it toward the out-of-pocket maximum;
- non-covered drugs;
- manufacturer assistance under the accumulator adjustment program.

## Cases (hypothetical member, individual maximum 3000.00)

| Out-of-pocket met before the claim | Out-of-pocket remaining | Cost share the covered claim would otherwise carry | Charged and posted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2900.00 | 100.00 | 40.00 | 40.00 |
| 2960.00 | 40.00 | 40.00 | 40.00 |
| 2980.00 | 20.00 | 40.00 | 20.00 (the claim crosses the maximum) |
| 3000.00 | 0.00 | 40.00 | 0.00 |

After the fourth row the member's covered claims for the rest of that plan year are charged zero member cost share. If one of those later fills also carries a brand-generic difference that the design does not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum, that difference is still charged.

## Points of judgement

- The zero charge lasts for the rest of the same plan year.
- Reaching the family maximum has the same effect for each family member as reaching the individual maximum.
- The posting for a crossing claim is the remainder, never the full cost share the claim would otherwise carry.
